# Donkey Development Kit

> An SDK for consuming Agent Fabric governance from Python agent code, without adopting Mule.

## Get started

- [Introduction](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/index.md): Governed by the gateway, understood by your code. DDK brings Agent Fabric and Omni Gateway awareness into your agent framework — typed refusals, budgets, telemetry and simulation, with native framework objects.
- [Quickstart](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/quickstart.md): (status: live) From pip install to a governed model call, a typed refusal, a budget and an OpenTelemetry span — locally, with no gateway and no credentials.
- [Feature overview](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/feature-overview.md): (status: live) Every DDK capability at a glance — its purpose, its goal, and what it saves developers — grouped by pillar.
- [Use with your coding agent](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/use-with-your-agent.md): (status: live) Point your coding assistant at these docs — llms.txt, llms-full.txt, and a .md next to every page — so it writes correct governed code.

## Models

- [Overview](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/frameworks.md): (status: live) Governed model access from eight agent frameworks. Each adapter returns the framework's own native model or client object, pointed at your Omni Gateway LLM proxy.
- [Gateway policies](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/frameworks/gateway-policies.md): (status: offline-verified) What each Omni Gateway policy on an LLM proxy does to a model call, the typed exception or field DDK gives your code for it, and how to rehearse it offline.
- [Routing & fallback](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/frameworks/routing.md): (status: live) How DDK reports the provider and model the gateway actually served, when a fallback answered, and how semantic routing and semantic caching show up on each response.
- [Version compatibility](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/frameworks/compatibility.md): (status: live) Which versions of each agent framework donkey-kit supports — the minimum, the version every PR tests, and known incompatibilities.

## Frameworks

- [LangGraph](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/frameworks/langgraph.md): (status: live) Use a governed LangChain ChatOpenAI in LangGraph, pointed at your Omni Gateway LLM proxy with full header and transport injection, typed refusals, and conformance testing.
- [OpenAI Agents SDK](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/frameworks/openai.md): (status: live) Use a governed OpenAIChatCompletionsModel in the OpenAI Agents SDK, backed by a pre-built AsyncOpenAI client pointed at your Omni Gateway LLM proxy.
- [Google ADK](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/frameworks/adk.md): (status: live) Use a governed LiteLlm model, or ADK's native Gemini model on a Format=Gemini proxy, in Google's Agent Development Kit (ADK), pointed at your Omni Gateway LLM proxy.
- [Strands](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/frameworks/strands.md): (status: live) Use a governed OpenAIModel in Strands Agents, pointed at your Omni Gateway LLM proxy with full header and transport injection.
- [MS Agent Framework](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/frameworks/agent-framework.md): (status: live) Use a governed OpenAIChatClient in Microsoft Agent Framework, pointed at your Omni Gateway LLM proxy, with policy middleware that ends a run on a typed governance refusal.
- [Anthropic SDK](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/frameworks/anthropic.md): (status: live) Use a governed AsyncAnthropic client with the Anthropic SDK, pointed at a Format=Anthropic Omni Gateway LLM proxy with full header and transport injection.
- [CrewAI](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/frameworks/crewai.md): (status: live) Use a governed CrewAI LLM, served by CrewAI's native OpenAI provider and pointed at your Omni Gateway LLM proxy.
- [LlamaIndex](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/frameworks/llamaindex.md): (status: live) Use a governed OpenAILike LLM in LlamaIndex, pointed at your Omni Gateway LLM proxy with is_chat_model forced on.

## MCP tools

- [Overview](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/tool-access.md): (status: live) Discover the governed MCP tools your organisation publishes in Exchange and bind them into any framework as native tool objects.
- [Discovery, search & filter](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/tool-access/discovery.md): (status: live) Find governed MCP tools by governance criteria, domain and tags, search the registry by name, asset type and environment, and see why any tool was included or excluded.
- [Framework binding](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/tool-access/binding.md): (status: live) Turn discovered governed MCP servers into each framework's native tool objects, with auth, lifecycle, name collisions, and filtering handled for you.
- [Pinning & lockfile](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/tool-access/lockfile.md): (status: offline-verified) Pin the tools each governed MCP server lists in a donkey.lock, so a catalog change becomes a typed ToolLockDrift and a reviewable diff instead of a runtime surprise.
- [Gateway policies](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/tool-access/gateway-policies.md): (status: offline-verified) Consume policy-shaped MCP catalogs and handle gateway refusals without guessing policy identity or reimplementing enforcement.

## A2A agents

- [Overview](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/a2a.md): (status: offline-verified) Everything DDK does for agent-to-agent (A2A) calls, in one place. Serve and expose your agent behind the gateway, call other governed agents, and handle what the gateway enforces.
- [Serve & expose](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/a2a/serve.md): (status: offline-verified) Make your agent callable by other agents over A2A — serve it in one line, expose it through the gateway, and develop against a gateway on your laptop.
- [Call other agents](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/a2a/call.md): (status: offline-verified) Send official A2A SDK requests to registry-resolved governed agents, with scoped authentication and context-managed streams.
- [Gateway policies](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/a2a/gateway-policies.md): (status: offline-verified) Version-specific A2A gateway policy captures, DDK outcomes, and offline replay and telemetry boundaries.

## Governance (all surfaces)

- [Typed refusals](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/errors.md): (status: live) Typed exceptions for every governance refusal, each with a discriminator, a retry rule, and a next step.
- [Refusal handlers](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/refusal-handlers.md): (status: live) Register a reaction to a typed refusal once, and the transport applies it to every governed call. A handler reacts; it never turns a refusal into a success.
- [Custom policies](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/custom-policies.md): (status: live) Map your own gateway policy's refusal to a typed exception with classify.register(), so it reaches your code, handlers and spans like a built-in refusal.
- [Budget & pacing](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/budget.md): (status: live) Remaining token budget as a first-class object, with pacing that slows down before it hits the wall.
- [Identity](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/identity.md): (status: live) On-behalf-of user identity, so the gateway can enforce per-user policy instead of seeing only the service.

## Human-in-the-loop

- [Overview](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/hitl.md): (status: live) Declare on the tool that a human must approve the call. DDK pauses it, records who decided, and runs it on approval. The approval is client-side and advisory.
- [In your framework](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/hitl/frameworks.md): (status: live) How the framework approval helpers pause a tool call for a human in LangGraph, the OpenAI Agents SDK, Strands and Google ADK, and resume it on approval.
- [Gateway step-up & challenges](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/hitl/gateway-step-up.md): (status: live) Gateway step-up and A2A Authorization-Code challenges, plus the discovered-tools approval. The gateway holds a call until a person approves it.

## Governance (all surfaces)

- [Policy handshake](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/policies.md): (status: roadmap) Read the in-force policy set to avoid calls that will be refused — advisory only; the gateway always wins.

## Observability

- [OpenTelemetry spans](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/telemetry.md): (status: live) OpenTelemetry GenAI spans for every governed call, in the dashboard you already run, and how DDK's own debug logging works.
- [Correlation IDs](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/correlation.md): (status: live) Per-run correlation IDs, carried on the wire, on every span and on every exception, and how they join gateway records across agent hops.
- [Cost attribution](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/cost-attribution.md): (status: live) Per-call cost tags (team, project, env, enduser.id) on every model span, where they go on the wire and in the gateway's records, and how to attribute spend per request.

## Local simulator

- [Overview](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/simulator.md): (status: live) Run a local server that replays real gateway rejections, so you can build and test failure handling without a governed gateway.
- [MCP faults & captures](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/simulator/mcp.md): (status: live) Refuse MCP tool calls on cue with simulate_mcp(), and replay packaged MCP gateway captures, so tool-refusal handling is tested without a governed gateway.
- [A2A faults & replay](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/simulator/a2a.md): (status: live) Refuse outbound A2A calls on cue with simulate_a2a(), and replay captured A2A ingress refusals in front of your own agent, without a governed gateway.

## Build, test & ship

- [Testing & conformance](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/testing.md): (status: live) Test your agent's failure handling — in-process refusal injection, a pytest conformance suite you run against your own agent, and an out-of-process gateway fixture.
- [Decorators](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/decorators.md): (status: live) The @donkey.governed, @donkey.tool and @donkey.agent decorators, and what each one does to the function it wraps.

## CLI

- [Overview & reference](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/cli.md): (status: live) The donkey CLI, with global flags, exit codes, JSON output and the generated command reference. Each command is on the page for its workflow stage.
- [Set up](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/cli/setup.md): (status: live) donkey init and donkey doctor set up a project's connection and configuration, and check that the setup is right.
- [Develop locally](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/cli/local.md): (status: live) donkey mock, donkey dev and donkey test run your agent against the local simulator, a dev card and the offline test suite.
- [Ship](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/cli/ship.md): (status: live) From code to a publish plan, then donkey scan, scaffold, publish, verify and expose, the commands that take an agent from code to Exchange.

## Scan & publish

- [Overview](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/publishing.md): (status: live) donkey scan derives a deterministic model of your agents, tools and MCP servers from code; publishing registers it with Exchange / Agent Registry from CI, complementing Agent Scanners.
- [CI pipelines](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/publishing/ci.md): (status: live) Run donkey publish from GitHub Actions, GitLab CI or Bitbucket Pipelines, with the same plan, artifact and exit code on each provider.
- [Publication & verify()](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/publishing/publication.md): (status: live) The Publication object, descriptor derivation, and verify(), the read-only runtime check that a live MCP server or A2A agent still matches its published version.

## Build, test & ship

- [Troubleshooting](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/troubleshooting.md): (status: live) How to read donkey doctor output, tell apart failures that look the same, explain an UNAVAILABLE donkey.last_call, and fix a 401 in JWT mode.

## Scenarios

- [Overview](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/scenarios.md): (status: live) Three end-to-end walkthroughs — support triage, an overnight batch job, and an internal copilot — each showing the governance layer a bare base_url cannot give you.
- [Support triage](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/scenarios/support-triage.md): (status: offline-verified) Draft replies to a queue of support tickets, one carrying PII, with typed refusals, correlation IDs, and OTel spans — the shipped LangGraph demo, end to end, no gateway.
- [Support triage (Agents SDK)](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/scenarios/support-triage-agents-sdk.md): (status: offline-verified) The support-triage scenario on the second deep adapter — an OpenAI Agents SDK Agent under Runner.run drafts ticket replies, the PII-laden one comes back as a typed refusal, no gateway.
- [Nightly batch](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/scenarios/nightly-batch.md): (status: live) Enrich tens of thousands of records overnight against a windowed token budget, unattended — pacing before the wall and resuming after the window resets, tested end to end against the simulator.
- [Internal copilot](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/scenarios/internal-copilot.md): (status: live) An internal assistant whose output must clear a content-safety guardrail — the ContentSafetyBlocked branch driven by the simulator, with per-run correlation joining the refusal to your logs.

## Examples

- [Overview](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/examples.md): (status: live) Runnable DDK examples from the companion demos repo — narrative demos that run offline against the local simulator, and short per-framework scripts for a live gateway.

## General

- [Governed client](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/examples/general/governed-client.md): (status: live) A stock OpenAI client next to a governed one, the same PII refusal through both, and the @donkey.governed / @donkey.tool decorators.
- [Typed refusals](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/examples/general/typed-refusals.md): (status: live) Every captured gateway rejection shape mapped to a typed exception with classify(), live refusals on a blocking client, and GatewayUnavailable when nothing answers.
- [Budget & pacing](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/examples/general/budget-and-pacing.md): (status: live) The gateway's token window as an object, pace(reserve=) refusing locally before a request would cross your reserve, and wait_for_reset().
- [Simulating refusals](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/examples/general/simulating-refusals.md): (status: live) Run the refusal branch of your agent without a gateway — donkey.simulate() in-process, and donkey mock --scenario for a stock client.
- [Conformance suite](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/examples/general/conformance.md): (status: live) pytest --donkey-conformance grading an agent's refusal handling, budget retries and correlation logging — first a naive agent, then the fixed one, then exemptions.
- [Telemetry](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/examples/general/telemetry.md): (status: live) OpenTelemetry GenAI spans with no instrumentation code, one correlation id per donkey.run(), refusal spans, and zero-config OTLP export.
- [Framework objects & model handles](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/examples/general/framework-objects.md): (status: offline-verified) Framework adapters that return your framework's own objects, connection_kwargs() for the rest, local model capability handles, and config validation that reports everything at once.
- [LangGraph agent](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/examples/general/langgraph-agent.md): (status: offline-verified) A real LangGraph tool-calling agent governed end to end — LangChain's own ChatOpenAI, one run id around the loop, and typed refusals out of astream.
- [Gateway identity (last_call)](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/examples/general/gateway-identity.md): (status: live) donkey.last_call on a successful call — which gateway served it, what it routed to, per-call token usage — and on_model_substitution="raise" turning a silent model swap into ModelSubstituted.

## Examples

- [OpenAI](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/examples/openai.md): (status: offline-verified) Sixteen straight-line scripts for the stock openai client governed by donkey.openai() — last_call, typed refusals, budget pacing, spans, decorators, streaming, guardrails, JWT wallets and the local simulator.
- [LangGraph](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/examples/langgraph.md): (status: offline-verified) Nine LangGraph scripts — a real ChatOpenAI on /chat/completions, typed refusals out of create_agent, the run id reaching tools, streaming, spans and the local simulator.
- [OpenAI Agents SDK](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/examples/openai-agents.md): (status: offline-verified) Three OpenAI Agents SDK scripts — an OpenAIResponsesModel on the governed client, a tool-calling Runner, typed refusals and the local simulator.
- [MS Agent Framework](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/examples/agent-framework.md): (status: offline-verified) Three Microsoft Agent Framework scripts — an OpenAIChatClient built by donkey.agent_framework, typed refusals unwrapped from ChatClientException, and the local simulator.
- [Strands](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/examples/strands.md): (status: offline-verified) Four Strands Agents scripts — OpenAIModel on a pre-built governed client, the run id reaching a tool, typed refusals simulated and live.
- [CrewAI](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/examples/crewai.md): (status: offline-verified) Two CrewAI scripts — donkey.crewai.llm() for a direct call and a one-agent crew, and typed refusals from CrewAI's native OpenAI provider.
- [LlamaIndex](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/examples/llamaindex.md): (status: offline-verified) Two LlamaIndex scripts — an OpenAILike from donkey.llamaindex.llm() for complete() and chat(), and typed refusals from its unchanged openai errors.
- [Google ADK](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/examples/adk.md): (status: offline-verified) Two Google ADK scripts — a LiteLlm model from donkey.adk.model() in an InMemoryRunner, and a PII refusal raised outside donkey.run(), where it stays LiteLLM's error.
- [Anthropic](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/examples/anthropic.md): (status: offline-verified) Two scripts for the native anthropic client from donkey.anthropic.client() — /v1/messages on a Format=Anthropic proxy with last_call, and typed refusals simulated in-process.
- [Gemini](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/examples/gemini.md): (status: offline-verified) Two plain-httpx scripts against a Format=Gemini proxy — native generateContent, and an OpenAI-shaped request classified as UpstreamRequestError.

## Configuration

- [Overview & all settings](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/reference/configuration.md): (status: live) Every DDK configuration value — LLM proxy URL and credentials, JWT model-wallet auth, attribution, cost tags, telemetry, and Anypoint control-plane settings — as env vars, config file, or code.
- [Auth modes](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/reference/configuration/auth.md): (status: live) How DDK authenticates to the LLM proxy, with client ID enforcement, your own provider key, JWT model-wallet mode, bearer tokens and auth providers.
- [Attribution, telemetry & behaviour](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/reference/configuration/attribution.md): (status: live) Application attribution, correlation and cost-attribution headers, telemetry switches, and behaviour settings such as tool-set size warnings and value checks.
- [Control plane & credentials](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/reference/configuration/control-plane.md): (status: live) The Anypoint control-plane settings, and which credentials and headers the SDK sends to each host.

## Reference

- [Python API](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/reference/api.md): (status: live) The public Python API of donkey-kit — Donkey, DonkeyConfig, the model client, the budget window, last_call, the adapters and every export — generated from the code.
- [last_call fields](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/reference/last-call.md): (status: live) Every field on donkey.last_call — the observability status, the gateway identity, the routing and fallback signals, the per-call token usage, and the semantic-cache outcome the gateway reported about the most recent governed model call.
- [Connected-app scopes](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/reference/scopes.md): (status: live) The Anypoint connected-app scopes each DDK operation needs, where to grant them, and what the SDK raises when one is missing.
- [Unsupported boundary](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/reference/unsupported-boundary.md): (status: live) Which MuleSoft platform APIs DDK calls, whether each is documented for third-party use, and the project's support statement.

## Reference & project

- [Release notes](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/release-notes.md): Where the donkey-kit release notes live, what each one covers, and how to check which version you have installed and which one these docs describe.
- [Roadmap](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/roadmap.md): Where DDK is going — five phases in order, each with its goal, live progress and the issues in its milestone.

## Community

- [Team](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/community/team.md): The people behind the Donkey Development Kit — its creators and contributors.
- [Contribute](https://docs.donkey-kit.dev/community/contribute.md): How to contribute to DDK — issues, docs, examples and code — from filing an issue to a merged pull request.
